uutiset.t: Congo Pitches $15 Billion Infrastructure Deals as Mining Booms
uutiset.s: Democratic Republic of Congo is pitching $15 billion in rail and other infrastructure projects as it rides a copper mining boom that the government hopes will transform trade and transport in the central African nation.

uutiset.t: BBVA Weighs SRT to Hedge About $500 Million of Data Center Loans
uutiset.s: BBVA SA is considering a deal that would offload risk on about €500 million ($547 million) of data center loans, as banks worldwide explore multiple ways to hedge their exposure to artificial intelligence-related infrastructure.

uutiset.t: Congo Closes on Top Copper Supplier Chile as Exports Soar Again
uutiset.s: The Democratic Republic of Congo is closing the gap on the world’s top copper producer Chile, after quarterly exports topped 1 million tons for the first time in the three months through September.

uutiset.t: Inflation-Wary Shoppers Prepare for Black Friday
uutiset.s: Retailers had plenty of reasons to be worried about this year’s holiday season, but the latest round of earnings, from Dick’s Sporting Goods Inc. to Kohl’s Corp. and Dollar Tree Inc., show that shoppers are still spending briskly, despite their concerns about rising costs. Bloomberg's Shaquille Omar

uutiset.t: China’s Copper Crunch Hides a Fragile Demand Outlook
uutiset.s: A near-term supply squeeze is more easily fixed than weaker economic growth.

uutiset.t: Trump’s China Tariffs Threaten Fresh Trade Tensions
uutiset.s: China has vowed to defend its interests after the US unveiled new tariffs on Chinese goods and warned the rate could double if trade talks collapse, injecting fresh tension ahead of a planned meeting between Donald Trump and Xi Jinping. Stocks rose as investors in Europe and Asia tracked a comeback

uutiset.t: Turkey Plans Lower Taxes on Lira Deposits to Support Currency
uutiset.s: Turkey is planning to lower taxes on interest from lira deposits to support demand for the currency following a sharp decline in official foreign-exchange reserves, according to people familiar with the matter.

uutiset.t: AlexForbes Sees More Growth After Assets Hit $45 Billion
uutiset.s: South Africa’s biggest commercial retirement-fund administrator boosted assets under management 13% in the first half and expects to maintain that pace for the rest of the year.

uutiset.t: Malaysia Says May Intervene If AirAsia’s Financial Woes Worsen
uutiset.s: Malaysia may consider stepping in to support AirAsia Group Bhd. if the airline’s financial difficulties worsen, Second Finance Minister Amir Hamzah Azizan said, as the government seeks to protect domestic air connectivity.

uutiset.t: UniCredit Clears Final Hurdle to Take Over Commerzbank
uutiset.s: UniCredit proposed CEO Andrea Orcel as Commerzbank chairman, as the Italian lender moves to take control of its German rival in one of Europe’s largest banking deals in decades. Bloomberg's Steven Arons reports. (Source: Bloomberg)

uutiset.t: Couche-Tard Sees Zabka Model Expanding Beyond Poland, Romania
uutiset.s: Alimentation Couche-Tard Inc. envisions taking Zabka Group SA’s convenience-store model into more European markets as the Canadian retailer prepares to complete its biggest-ever acquisition.

uutiset.t: Wall Street Flips From AI Euphoria to Gloom
uutiset.s: US stocks haven’t been this volatile in years.

uutiset.t: Coris’ Ivory Coast Bank Unit Plans IPO in Push for Top Five
uutiset.s: Coris Holding SA’s Ivory Coast unit plans a 62.7 billion CFA franc ($105 million) initial public offering as the lender seeks to broaden its investor base and break into the country’s top five banks.

uutiset.t: Romanian Far-Right Leader Simion Charged With Inciting Violence
uutiset.s: Romanian far-right leader George Simion was charged with public incitement by prosecutors for allegedly urging violence against election bureau justices last year following the highly-contested 2024 presidential election.

uutiset.t: Vietnam Weighs Delaying Nuclear Power Plants Beyond 2035
uutiset.s: Vietnam may be forced to delay its first nuclear power plants until after 2035, complicating efforts to boost energy security and economic growth.
